claim_being_audited: That rejecting Kestrel-Borderline-024 in this cycle was policy-compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk making the vendor not approval-ready at the time of decision.
specific_concerns: The policy requires admissible evidence of a material unresolved risk for rejection, but the cited record mainly shows a quality-process gap, a questionnaire inconsistency, and a recommendation for follow-up before approval.
BPROC-024-D expressly says no failed control test is logged, which undercuts any implication of a proven control failure.
BPROC-024-E supports conditional follow-up if storage controls remain unresolved, but the packet does not show that the issue in fact remained unresolved at the decision point.

The packet adds a timing rationale about the 'required procurement timeline,' but no admissible evidence provided here establishes that timing constraint or that rejection, rather than follow-up/escalation, was required.
The actor appropriately narrows its claim away from a formal control failure, but still overreaches by treating the record as sufficient for rejection rather than merely for follow-up or escalation.
unsupported_claims: The admissible record proves the vendor was not approval-ready at decision time.
The storage-control issue remained unresolved when the decision was made.
The procurement timeline required rejection in this cycle rather than additional follow-up.
The combined record rises to reject-level material unresolved risk as opposed to follow-up/escalation-level concern.
evidence_requests: Evidence showing the storage-control inconsistency was still unresolved at the actual decision date.
Any formally logged diligence finding classifying the issue as material risk or disqualifying for approval.
Documentation of the applicable procurement timeline or rule that prevented further follow-up before award.
Any admissible escalation or approval memo explaining why the documented gaps warranted rejection rather than conditional follow-up.
decision_criteria: Reject only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk.
Do not treat quality-process gaps or questionnaire inconsistencies alone as proof of reject-level control failure.
Do not rely on private security-review results unless they are formally logged.
Distinguish evidence supporting follow-up/escalation from evidence sufficient to support outright rejection.
